text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- Russian AutoVAZ car makers publically admitted low quality of their product.
- The government prepared a number of 'unorthodox' ways to pay wages arrears to all public sector workers. These measures are said to include introduction of VAT on alluminium export.
- Russian IFCI Bank is to merge with Renaissance Capital company.
- Moscow tries to distance itself from a scandal around last week's signing of an oil agreement with Azerbaijan.
- Despite a new law liberalising prescious metalls market in Russia, individuals have little incentive to buy gold bars because of unclear situation with VAT.
- YUKOS oil company is to undergo further structural changes.
SEVODNYA
- New Central Bank regulations are to lower clients' risks.
- Russians are not likely to buy gold as willingly as they buy U.S. dollars, experts say.
- Tyumen Oil Company stake's initial price at the forthcoming auction may go up by one trillion roubles, sources with the Fuel and Energy Ministry say.
- The government is unhappy about the way the budget money is spent in the regions.
- The State Duma lower house of the parliament, natural monopolies and regional authorities successfully resist the government's new reform programme.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia may only comfort itself with the fact that NATO's eastwards expansion does not include two more East European countries, says the paper's analysis of the NATO summit in Madrid.
- Chechnya has a chance to dictate its conditions to Russia using advantages of an oil deal with Azerbaijan.
PRAVDA-5
- Russian authorities have run out of the space for a policy of manoeuvring, the Kremlin's opponent says.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
